topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks introduce the lecture, establish the importance and reputation of complement, and set expectations for the session.

topics.label: Overview, nomenclature, and central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental architecture, naming conventions, and central role of C3 in the complement system.

topics.label: Mechanisms of complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three pathways of complement activation and how they converge to deposit C3b and reach the trigger threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the downstream effector outcomes of complement activation, including opsonization, inflammation, and membrane attack complex lysis.

topics.label: Host regulation and protection against complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory mechanisms and factors that protect host cells from complement-mediated damage.

topics.label: Clinical manifestations of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the diverse disease phenotypes and clinical consequences associated with deficiencies in specific complement components and regulators.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the molecular strategies and evolutionary mechanisms pathogens use to evade complement destruction, illustrated by Staphylococcus aureus.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks conclude the complement lecture and preview the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
